chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When the person in ihram is compelled to wear a qaba' (a coat with sleeves) and finds no other garment besides it, let him wear it inside out and not insert his hands into the sleeves of the qaba'."

key_terms.الْقَبَاءِ: A type of coat with sleeves
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for wearing a sleeved coat during Hajj if no other garment is available?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the practical necessity (*darura*) of wearing a *qaba'* (sleeved coat) when no other garment is available, a common scenario in the harsh climates of the Hijaz. By instructing the pilgrim to wear it inside out and keep hands out of the sleeves, the Imam ensures the garment remains distinct from the prohibited 'sewn garments' (*thawb al-mukhallas*) while maximizing comfort and minimizing the extent of the exception. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of balancing strict adherence to ritual purity with the alleviation of hardship.
